storyboard.claim: A free day is a full 24 hours with no work at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A closed door at home, the worker relaxed on the other side of it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the chunk's list of the three calendar day types into free days.
storyboard.addedInformation: Home shows the free day is spent away from the office.
storyboard.staging: Everyman relaxed at home, face open: rest, not work.

storyboard.claim: The host likes the free day but already hesitates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person pausing mid-thought at a desk, weighing an idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Right after the free day definition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the objection is coming.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking, uneasy: a doubt forming, not shock.

storyboard.claim: The speaker is about to argue against the no-meeting Wednesday idea.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person pointing across the room, playfully challenging.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from liking the idea to challenging it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the role the speaker takes: opposing the idea on purpose.
storyboard.staging: Everyman points with a knowing smirk: a challenge, not a threat.

storyboard.claim: Blocking Wednesday could push all meetings onto Tuesday and Thursday.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: empty Wednesday, compressed meetings, Thursday burnout.
storyboard.onScreenText: Wednesday is empty, and Thursday burns out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The devil's advocate objection, spelled out as a chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause and effect of the objection.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking over the chain: the worry is the objection itself.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that meetings disappear when Wednesday is blocked.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tired person slumped at a desk, with the rejected idea struck through in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the objection from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the idea as wrong, not as a fact.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumped and worried under the struck-through claim.

storyboard.claim: The same workload is squeezed into fewer days, so the burden is not reduced.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person holding a stack of notes, slumped under a full workload.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the meetings do not vanish.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes show a full load of work, not one lighter day.
storyboard.staging: Everyman carrying a heavy stack of notes, slumped.

storyboard.claim: The real purpose of no-meeting Wednesday is not to cut the number of meetings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person pointing at a struck-through goal in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Corrects the objection by naming the true goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the common assumption as the wrong purpose.
storyboard.staging: Everyman pointing, neutral: a correction, not an emotion.

storyboard.claim: After an interruption, the brain needs 20 to 25 minutes to reach deep concentration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person at a workstation, pausing to refocus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the goal of a contiguous block of time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the concrete cost of an interruption.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking at a workstation, refocusing.

storyboard.claim: Short meetings with gaps never let a person reach deep focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tired person slumped at a desk between fragmented meeting slots.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how a chopped-up Tuesday fails focus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the meeting pattern to the focus cost.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumped, worried: the fragmented day drains focus.

storyboard.claim: Wednesday delivers eight uninterrupted hours of high-value output.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person celebrating at a workstation after a productive stretch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payoff of the Wednesday block.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a number on the payoff.
storyboard.staging: Everyman celebrating: genuine accomplishment.

storyboard.claim: Deep work solves hard problems and produces real documents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb icon above a person holding notes after finishing a strategy document.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives examples of the eight-hour payoff.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lightbulb reads as a solved idea.
storyboard.staging: Everyman celebrating with a finished document in hand.

storyboard.claim: The productivity gain is larger than the cost of a chaotic Thursday.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance scale icon with a person weighing the two sides.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Weighs the payoff against the cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scale shows a comparison of two sides.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking over the scale: a judgment of the trade-off.

storyboard.claim: Enduring a shallow Thursday protects the deep Wednesday.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon held by a person, guarding a single day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the trade-off as a choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection of the block.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holding a shield, talking: a deliberate choice.

storyboard.claim: Time is a decision about when to go deep, not a scheduling task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person pointing at the choice they must make.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the trade-off as a decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the schedule into a choice the viewer makes.
storyboard.staging: Everyman pointing at a choice: the decision is theirs.

storyboard.claim: Deep work needs fuel, so energy management matters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tired person slumped at a desk, recognizable as the familiar afternoon slump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from time to the energy that fuels it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the topic shift to energy.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumped and worried: the familiar energy crash.

storyboard.claim: At 3 p.m. a designer sits staring blankly at a glowing monitor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person at a workstation, eyes empty, facing a glowing screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the midday energy example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the blank state of low energy.
storyboard.staging: Everyman blank-faced before the monitor: apathy from exhaustion.

storyboard.claim: The worker reaches for another coffee to push through the slump.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person reaching for a cup of coffee at a desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the midday scene with the caffeine attempt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cup is the literal sign of forcing energy.
storyboard.staging: Everyman reaching for a cup with a tired, sad face.

storyboard.claim: Trying to squeeze productivity from an exhausted person is hopeless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worn-out person slumped at a workstation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the fumes image into the sponge metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout states the metaphor in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Everyman drained and slumped: running on empty.

storyboard.claim: The midday slump is where time management shifts from psychology to physiology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person at an office desk in the middle of the day, mid-thought.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the midday example as a turning point.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the slump as a body problem, not a mindset problem.
storyboard.staging: Everyman pausing at the wall, worried.

storyboard.claim: A day has a fixed number of minutes, so time cannot be added.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon with the fixed day length stated.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the energy argument by ruling out more time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact total of minutes in a day.
storyboard.staging: Everyman neutral beside the clock: a plain fact.

storyboard.claim: Energy is the one thing a person can actually change.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person pointing at a single lever-like choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the fixed-minutes point with the one variable left.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names energy as the only variable.
storyboard.staging: Everyman pointing at the one thing to adjust.

storyboard.claim: The industrial revolution taught people to act like machines running eight flat hours.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person thinking about a long unbroken workday.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains where the eight-hour grind idea came from.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the machine model as the wrong model for people.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking, uneasy about the machine idea.

storyboard.claim: Working past peak energy leads to diminishing returns.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: peak energy, pushing past it, diminishing returns.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the biological rhythm cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the chain from peak to lower output.
storyboard.staging: Everyman talking over the chain: an explanation.

storyboard.claim: A task that should take 20 minutes can take an hour and a half when energy drops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz at a workstation, straining over a single task.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the cost of working past peak energy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a concrete time on the agony of effort.
storyboard.staging: Cruz worried and thinking over a stalled task.

storyboard.claim: The most productive people work in pulses with pauses, not continuous grinding.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person at ease, between bursts of work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the alternative to grinding.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the rhythm the best workers use.
storyboard.staging: Everyman calm: a rhythm, not a grind.

storyboard.claim: A productive person builds a sensory cocoon before deep work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person seated at a workstation, settled in for focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the example of focused sprints.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the setup used before sprints.
storyboard.staging: Everyman settled and content at a workstation.

storyboard.claim: The cocoon starts with an app that blocks distracting websites.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon with a person holding a phone, blocking sites.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the first part of the cocoon.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone shows the blocking happens in an app.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holding the phone: the app is the tool.

storyboard.claim: Binaural beats play two slightly different tones, one into each ear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person explaining sound going to each ear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the next part of the cocoon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines binaural beats in one line.
storyboard.staging: Everyman talking, neutral: an explanation.

storyboard.claim: The brain creates a third, phantom 10 Hz frequency from the two tones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person thinking about a tone that is not played.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the exact example of the difference tone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the phantom frequency and its value.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinking: the tone is heard, not played.

storyboard.claim: Using sound aims to force the brain into a relaxed, focused flow state.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person thinking with a calm, focused posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the phantom tone to alpha and theta focus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the goal of the sound: flow.
storyboard.staging: Everyman focused and calm: the target state.

storyboard.claim: A 50-minute timer sets the length of each intense work sprint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person holding an hourglass, marking the sprint length.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the timer after the beats are set.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact sprint length.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holding the hourglass: a fixed block of time.

storyboard.claim: When the timer ends the worker stops completely, four times a day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person seated and stopping work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the timer with the stop.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the four-sprint daily total.
storyboard.staging: Everyman seated, stopped: a firm end.

storyboard.claim: The worker claims up to four times the output of a normal grinding day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coin stack beside a person celebrating the output of a full day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the payoff of the sprints.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy shows the claimed win, which is stated as a claim.
storyboard.staging: Everyman celebrating the claimed gain.

storyboard.claim: Peak productivity rises and falls like a wave: surge, then recover.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person explaining the rise and fall of output.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the sprint pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the wave image for surge and rest.
storyboard.staging: Everyman talking: the summary of the pattern.

storyboard.claim: After 50 to 90 minutes of work, a short deliberate break recharges the worker.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person seated and relaxed during a break.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the break length after the sprints.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact break length.
storyboard.staging: Everyman relaxed on a genuine break.

storyboard.claim: Most people do not take a real five-minute break.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person talking, frank and concerned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the ideal break to the real one.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the gap between ideal and actual breaks.
storyboard.staging: Everyman frank and worried: an honest admission.

storyboard.claim: When a hard task ends, people minimize the document and pick up something else.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person holding notes, having just put the work away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the common break habit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes stand for the work being hidden.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holding notes, neutral: the work set aside.

callout.text: JUST GIVE MY BRAIN A REST

storyboard.claim: People reach for social feeds during breaks, believing it is rest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon with a person holding a phone, smirking at the excuse.
storyboard.onScreenText: JUST GIVE MY BRAIN A REST
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what the break becomes in practice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone is the modern feed; the smirk marks the false excuse.
storyboard.staging: Everyman smirking at the phone: the self-deception.

storyboard.claim: A five-minute break turns into 45 minutes of doomscrolling and leaves the person more exhausted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person slumped, afraid, after losing time to a feed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the outcome of the phone break.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact lost time.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumped and afraid: the cost of the scroll.

storyboard.claim: A screen break is not an energy break, because the brain keeps processing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A blank-faced person holding a phone, the empty contrast to rest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the break argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the idea that a screen break restores energy.
storyboard.staging: Everyman blank beside the phone: empty, not rested.
